issue.title: Reproduce lemma 6b1(5) on win2

labels.name: win2

milestone.description: Wire the review's control fixes into the M = 5 certificate, certify lemmas 6a(5) and 6b1, review them independently, and write up Theorem A(M = 5).

issue.body:
**What.** Reproduce lemma 6b₁(5) on win2, with its own python-flint build: the C¹ ray, all 18 rows and the covering check on p̂ ± 1e-18, as #37 and #38 ran it on macm3 (raw `I38-macm3/`, 8e2ba33). Recommended by macm3 in #38's summary.

**Why.** The certificate rests on one machine and one build. #111's criterion: the rerun passes when its own covering check passes. Its balls may differ from macm3's in their radii.

**Commands (win2, beside #82; main at c282ab8 or later).** Raw folder `I121-win2` (README first line `# I121-win2: lemma 6b1(5) reproduced on win2`, with the python-flint and FLINT versions). From `solver/proof/`:
```
set X=2.71857918921174241298383648012843280883,0.99922840320656778341382852244561290493,0.14920357491144750568385993252030607895,0.01471905249025135288037099322184756733,0.00840534690576166107173716067740959800,0.00147034518159157802673581431742815600
python -u lemma6b1_cover_M.py ray --M=5 --c1 --x=%X% --h=1e-18 --tag=_cert > <raw>\I121-win2\ray.log 2>&1
```
Then five parallel `rows` processes, `--only=0,10,15`, `1,12,16`, `2,11,13,17`, `3,4,14` and `5,6,7,8,9`, each with `--M=5 --x=%X% --h=1e-18 --tag=_cert`. After them come `check` with `--json`, `check --drop=9,5` (must fail) and `mutate --j=0` (must certify no disc), as in #38's body. Copy `lemma6b1_runs_M5_cert/` into the raw folder.

**Acceptance (can fail).** All 366 discs certify and `check` exits 0; the dropped-tile check fails; `mutate` certifies none. Max Λ and box radius per row are tabulated against #38's.

**Depends on.** #38 (closed).

- Raw folder: `I121-win2/`.

win2, 2026-11-08 06:57 UTC. Progress, and one process crash to report. No disc has failed.

**Done.** The C1 ray exited 0 in 588 s (06:19:42 to 06:29:30 UTC). Rows 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 11, 13 and 15 are saved and certified. `rows_a` (rows 0, 10, 15) exited 0 after 1587 s. Rows `c`, `d` and `e` are still running, and every disc so far reads `ok True`.

**Crash.** The `rows_b` process (`--only=1,12,16`) died silently in row 1 (|u| = 378.36), after disc 19/34 had printed `ok True, Lam 0.187, box radius 3.1e-16` at 358 s. Its log ends there, at 06:35:29 UTC, with no traceback. The chain's `wait` returned **exit 132**, which Git bash reports for a process killed by SIGILL, an illegal-instruction exception. Rows 12 and 16 of that group never started, and row 1 was not saved. This is a crash of the process, not a failing disc. Windows has no Application-log crash event for it.

The CPU is an Intel Core Ultra 7 265K with AVX2 and no AVX-512, and the same venv ran #104's 577 s lemma 6a run without trouble. I have not determined the cause.

**Recovery, for diagnosis.** At 06:57 UTC I ran the same `rows` command from the issue, narrowed to one row per process: `--only=1`, `--only=12` and `--only=16`, in parallel, with `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1` so that a native crash prints its stack. Nothing else differs, and the numerics are unchanged. The original crashed log stays as `rows_b.log`. The retry has its own guard (15 GB, 30 s). If row 1 crashes again, the stack will show where, and I will report it rather than keep retrying.

When the original chain finishes `c`, `d` and `e`, its `check` will fail because rows 1, 12 and 16 are missing. I will keep that output as a record and rerun `check`, `check --drop=9,5` and `mutate --j=0` after the retry.

Raw so far: `I121-win2/`.

win2, 2026-11-08 06:59 UTC. The CPU model and the event logs around the crash, as the coordinator asked.

**CPU.** Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 265K (GenuineIntel), 20 cores and 20 logical processors, 3.9 GHz maximum, AVX2 and no AVX-512. Windows 11 Pro build 26300.

**Events near the crash (06:35:29 UTC = 22:35:29 local).**
- The System and Application logs have **no event of any level between 06:25 and 06:45 UTC** apart from information entries (HTTP service, Universal Print, licensing). There is no Application Error, Application Hang, or Windows Error Reporting entry for a python.exe.
- There is **no WHEA-Logger event at all** since the boot of 04:30:06 UTC, so no corrected or uncorrected machine-check error was logged.
- One older fault is on record, and it is not the crash. At 04:30:26–04:30:28 UTC, in the first minute after the Windows Update restart, Windows Error Reporting filed a BlueScreen report (bugcheck 0x1E, exception code 0xC0000005, an access violation in kernel mode, on OS build 10.0.26100) and several LiveKernelEvent reports (codes 0x193 and 0x1A8). The same entries were filed again at 04:33 and 04:38 UTC. The build number (26100, not 26200 or 26300) suggests it came from the servicing phase of that update restart, not from a boot of this OS. I have not opened the dump, and it is 2 h before the crash.

A watcher checks that all 12 #82 processes and the retry are alive, so a native crash is seen within a minute and not only after a 3 h stall.

win2, 2026-11-08 07:31 UTC. Summary of #121. Lemma 6b₁(5) reproduces on win2: all 366 discs certify and the covering check passes. The result agrees with macm3's #38 in the disc counts, the Lohner step counts and max Λ, and the box radii agree to within 7 to 10%.

Environment: win2 (Windows 11 build 26300, Intel Core Ultra 7 265K), choptuik-venv, python-flint 0.9.0 with FLINT 3.6.0, Python 3.12.8. Worktree `..\choptuik-i121` at origin/main 58b048c, which contains c282ab8. Normal priority, threads pinned to 1, launched detached beside #82's twelve processes.

| `rows` b (1,12,16) | **132** | died in row 1 after disc 19/34, see below |

**Acceptance.** All three checks pass: every disc of rows 0 to 17 certifies and `check` exits 0, the dropped-tile check fails, and the mutation certifies none. Under #111's criterion the rerun passes when its own covering check passes.

**One process crash, reported and not fixed.** The `rows_b` process died at 06:35:29 UTC in row 1 after disc 19/34 (`ok True`), with exit 132 (SIGILL as Git bash reports it), no traceback and no Windows event. The original chain therefore stopped at "rows failed", and I ran the issue's three final commands by hand with the same arguments (`run_i121_final.sh`). Rows 1, 12 and 16 were rerun as three processes with `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1`; all three finished with exit 0, row 1 through disc 34/34, and the crash did not recur. The cause is not known. It is one of four native faults on win2 tonight, tabulated in my comment above and on #82. #121 was suspended from 07:02:01 to 07:05:13 UTC while Nathan decided, and resumed unchanged. Nathan's decision is to accept the fault risk, so these results count as confirmed because they agree with macm3's #38 here, an independent machine and build.

**Raw.** `I121-win2/`, raw-data commit 29582ad. It holds the logs of the ray, the five row processes, the retry and the three final steps, `lemma6b1_check_M5_cert.json`, `lemma6b1_runs_M5_cert/` (ray and 18 row files), `rows_table_vs_macm3.md` and the script that made it (its selftest plants a failed disc and finds it), `exits.txt`, the memory-guard logs and the README. `raw_check.py` passes on all of them.

**Recommended tasks.** None from this run. The repeat-and-compare test of win2's arithmetic is #140, already filed and running.
